question:
An engineer must configure Cisco IMC server management NIC for autonegotiation.
Which setting should be selected?
explanation: Auto-negotiation setting is only available in dedicated mode. This setting enables itself as long as a valid dedicated configuration is set.
theory: Auto-negotiation for the Cisco IMC management NIC is only available when the adapter is configured in dedicated mode, i.e., using a physically separate management port rather than sharing bandwidth with the LOM (shared LOM/shared LOM EXT) or riding on the Cisco VIC card. In dedicated mode the management NIC operates as an independent physical interface, which is what allows it to negotiate speed/duplex directly with its link partner; shared modes multiplex CIMC traffic onto a host NIC and don't expose the same negotiation setting. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco IMC Network Management)
